  THIS PORTION PROVIDES AN OPPORTUNITY FOR THE PUBLIC TO ADDRESS THE COUNCIL ON ITEMS
  WITHIN THE JURISDICTION OF THE COUNCIL AND NOT LISTED ON THE AGENDA. IF AN ITEM IS NOT ON THE
  AGENDA, THERE SHOULD BE NO SUBSTANTIAL DISCUSSION OF THE ISSUE BY THE COUNCIL, BUT COUNCIL
  MAY REFER THE MATTER TO STAFF OR SCHEDULE SUBSTANTIVE DISCUSSION FOR A FUTURE MEETING.
  (The Ralph M. Brown Act, Government Code Section 54954.2 (a).)

  CITY COUNCIL ORAL AND WRITTEN COMMUNICATION

  ITEMS TO BE REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR FOR SEPARATE ACTION.

  8.  APPROVAL OF THE WARRANT REGISTER
  Comments:
  City of Lynwood warrant register dated April 21, 2020 for FY 2019-2020. (FIN)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood approve the warrant register dated
  April 21, 2020 for FY 2019-2020.

  9.  QUARTERLY GENERAL LIABILITY CLAIM OVERVIEW
  Comments:
  Update status report General Liability Claims from December 2019 through February 2020. (HR)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood receive and file this quarterly
  general liability claims overview report.

  10.  PARKING ENFORCEMENT
  Comments:
  The City Council will receive a report on the Parking Enforcement unit including the objectives
  and responsibilities of parking enforcement. (CD)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file this report.  No further action is
  necessary.

  11.  ACCEPTANCE OF DECORATIVE MONUMENT SIGNAGE PROJECT
  Comments:
  The construction on the Decorative Monument Signage Project started on September 16, 2019.
  The Project was completed on November 12, 2019. Staff conducted the final inspection on
  November 12, 2019 and found that all work was completed in accordance with the project plans
  and specifications. The Project is ready for acceptance. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 2 of 97
   OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD ACCEPTING DECORATIVE
  MONUMENT SIGNAGE PROJECT (CIP NO. 4011.68.060) AS COMPLETE; AND
  AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF THE NOTICE OF COMPLETION WITH THE LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER’S OFFICE AND THE RELEASE OF THE 5%
  RETENTION 35 DAYS AFTER THE RECORDATION.”

  12.  APPROVAL OF ENERGY CONSERVATION PROJECTS FOR THE PURPOSE OF
  FILING OF THE NOTICES OF EXEMPTION
  Comments:
  In 2019, the City Council authorized the City Manager to proceed with implementation of projects
  that would include various energy savings measures. The project components have since been
  further developed and will include upgrades of lighting throughout the City to light emitting diode
  (LED) technology, potential installation of solar panels at various City facilities, and other energy
  saving measures associated with facility equipment.

  The various desired improvements have been evaluated in accordance with the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines and is has been determined that the projects
  qualify for exemption (categorical and/or statutory). Staff wishes to file an appropriate Notice of
  Exemption on the projects prior to the construction phase. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolutions entitled:

  “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING
  THE FINDING THAT THE DESIRED SOLAR PANELS AND REROOFING PROJECT
  QUALIFIES FOR AN EXEMPTION UNDER THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL
  QUALITY ACT (CEQA) GUIDELINES AND DIRECT STAFF TO FILE THE NOTICE OF
  EXEMPTION FOR THE SOLAR PANELS AND REROOFING PROJECT WITH LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY.”

  “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING
  THE FINDING THAT THE DESIRED ENERGY EFFICIENCY UPGRADES PROJECT
  QUALIFIES FOR AN EXEMPTION UNDER THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL
  QUALITY ACT (CEQA) GUIDELINES AND DIRECT STAFF TO FILE THE NOTICE OF
  EXEMPTION FOR THE CITYWIDE ENERGY EFFICIENCY UPGRADES PROJECT
  WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY.”

  13.  CONSIDERATION AND POSSIBLE ACTION TO ADOPT A RESOLUTION
  CONFIRMING CERTAIN ACTIONS COMPLETED BY THE CITY MANAGER IN
  RESPONSE TO THE DECLARATION OF A LOCAL EMERGENCY
  Comments:
  On April 10, 2020 the Lynwood City Manager issued the third public order to apply additional
  measures as the situation has evolved. In accordance with the Lynwood Municipal Code, any
  Public Orders issued by the City Manager is to be ratified by the City Council. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  It is recommended that the City Council adopt a Resolution confirming the public order issued by
  the City Manager in response to the declaration of a local emergency.

  NEW/OLD BUSINESS
  14.  ECONOMIC RELIEF PROGRAM FOR LYNWOOD RESIDENTS IMPACTED BY
  COVID-19
  Comments:

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 3 of 97
   The City wishes to implement a economic relief/recovery program(s) for Lynwood residents that
  have been impacted by COVID-19. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends for Council to review material and provide direction on a recovery program(s)
  to initiate for Lynwood residents.

  15.  AWARD OF CONTRACT AND APPROPRIATION FOR SANBORN AVENUE AND
  MULFORD AVENUE PARKING LOTS IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (CIP 4011.68.081)
  Comments:
  On March 17, 2019, the City Council took previous action to approve amendments to the City's
  FY 2020 Capital Improvement Budget. Included in those amendments were the Sanborn Avenue
  and Mulford Avenue Parking Lots, which required additional allocation of Lease Revenue bond
  funding to advance construction of the project. At that time the projects were identified as two
  separate projects; the projects are now proposed to be combined as a single project. (PW)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD AWARDING A CONTRACT TO
  ARAMEXX GROUP, INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF $326,434.80 FOR CONSTRUCTION OF A
  SINGLE SANBORN AVENUE AND MULFORD AVENUE PARKING LOTS
  IMPROVEMENT PROJECT AND AUTHORIZING AN APPROPRIATION IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $107,635 FROM LEASE REVENUE BOND FOR THE SANBORN AVENUE AND
  MULFORD AVENUE PARKING LOTS IMPROVEMENT PROJECT; AUTHORIZING THE
  MAYOR TO EXECUTE THE AGREEMENT”.

  16.  FISCAL YEAR (FY) 2019-20 BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS
  Comments:
  On July 2, 2019, the City Council adopted the FY 2019-20 budget and approved the FY 2020-21
  budget. The FY 2019-21 budget is the City’s financial operating plan that establishes the City’s
  goals, budget priorities, and desired service levels for the fiscal year, as well as identifies the
  fiscal resources necessary to achieve them. The adopted budget was based on certain
  assumptions and meeting expenditure and revenue projections. (FIN)
  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled, “A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING FY 2019-20 BUDGET
  ADJUSTMENTS AMENDING THE FY 2019-20 ADOPTED BUDGET HERETO
  ATTACHED AS SCHEDULE A”.
  ADJOURNMENT
  THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING WILL BE HELD ON MAY 5, 2020 AT 6:00 P.M. IN THE
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS OF THE CITY HALL ANNEX, 11350 BULLIS ROAD, CITY OF
  LYNWOOD, CALIFORNIA.

  SUBJECT:  PARKING ENFORCEMENT

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file this report. No further action is necessary.

  Background:

  The City’s Parking Enforcement unit is one of three services offered by the Public Safety Division, which under
  Community Development Department. Comprehensive parking enforcement is important to the health, safety,
  and economic vitality of Lynwood. Parking enforcement plays a vital role in ensuring that the streets are used in
  the best interests of the community. The primary objectives of parking enforcement are:

  support the on-street parking system by equitably and consistently enforcing the parking regulations,
  encourage compliance of the City's parking regulations and California Vehicle Code,
  promote traffic and pedestrian safety,
  maximize the capacity of the existing parking supply through increased turnover,
  protect access needed for commerce and public convenience; clear freight loading zones of all day
  commuters to allow adequate delivery space for commercial businesses; provide for a more efficient
  delivery of goods and services, and
  enhance the quality of life in residential neighborhoods by keeping residential areas free of commercial
  businesses commuters and visitor parking.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  A well-designed parking enforcement effort enables the City to maximize its use of the existing parking supply.
  Parking Enforcement primary responsibility is to ensure that drivers comply with the Lynwood Municipal Code
  Chapter 7 “Vehicle and Traffic” parking laws, as well as the California Vehicle Code (CVC). Services are offered
  from 7:00 a.m. - 11:00 p.m., daily. Among the activities performed by Parking Enforcement unit:

  patrol a designated route or area of the City and enforce the City’s parking laws and CVC,

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 38 of 97
   issue citations to vehicles parked illegally (i.e. loading zone violations, no-parking zones, no-parking
  timeframes for street sweeping, fire lane violations, crosswalk violations, lawn/sidewalk violations, double
  parking, expired time zones, disabled parking, etc.), expiration of vehicle registration tags, inoperable
  vehicles, etc.,
  cite and impound vehicles parked in the same spot for longer than 72 hours,
  cite and impound vehicles blocking a driveway,
  cite and impound abandoned vehicles left on City streets,
  cite and impound vehicles bearing registration expired more than six (6) months,
  impound vehicles parked on a City street with five (5) or more unpaid parking citations,
  patrol established residential permit parking districts to deter non-resident parking,
  conduct vehicle abatements within private properties on vehicles deemed inoperative,
  respond to citizen parking complaint, and
  public relations; interpret policy/procedure to the public; assist public regarding location of streets, buildings
  and other points of interest around town.

  Again, the Parking Enforcement unit is one of three services offered under the Public Safety Division. City staff,
  under the title of Public Safety Officer (PSO), perform the different services of the Public Safety Division. When
  the Public Safety Division receives a call for service, it is not always possible for a PSO to be dispatched
  immediately as they may be in the middle of another assignment. However, all calls for service are responded to
  and reported on. It is not uncommon when dealing with a parking enforcement call for the issue to be resolved
  prior to a PSO’s arrival. Anytime when a PSO is dispatched to an area, they survey the entire area for any other
  violations that need to be addressed, which not only includes parking violations but also code enforcement or
  animal control violations. This enables the City to maximize use of existing resources and ensure all violations
  observed are addressed.

City Council Regular Meeting - Page 46 of 97
   Discussion and Analysis:

  The California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines include a list of classes of projects which have been
  determined not to have a significant effect on the environment and which shall, therefore, be exempt from the
  provisions of CEQA. City staff recommends that the City Council find that the improvements contemplated with
  this project and described further below, fall into Section 15301 of the CEQA Guidelines as Class 1 exemptions.
  Class 1 consists of the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alterations of
  existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features involving negligible
  or no expansion of use. Further, there are specific provisions within the CEQA that exempt the installation of a
  solar energy system on the roof of existing buildings or at existing parking lots.
  Pursuant to the Public Resources Code 21152(b), if a local agency determines that a project is not subject to this
  division pursuant to subdivision (b) of Section 21080 or pursuant to Section 21172, and the local agency approves
  or determines to carry out the project, the local agency may file a notice of exemption with the county clerk of the
  county in which the project will be located. The filing of the Notice of Exemption is a prudent step to ensure the City
  is better positioned for timely implementation of a project.
  A Notice of Exemption has been prepared for each project: Solar and Reroofing Project and the Citywide Energy
  Efficient Upgrades. They are attachment to this report. The Solar and Reroofing Project, as detailed in the attached
  NOE, could include installation of solar panels on roofs and carports at several facilities. The citywide energy efficient
  upgrades include street light retrofits, exterior lighting retrofits, HVAC replacement, transformer replacement and
  potential pool pump VFD installation across multiple facilities.
  The City received a loan from the California Energy Commission in the amount of $1,734,071, which will be used
  towards implementation of these energy savings measures.
  Staff recommends for the City Council to find that the projects are exempt from CEQA and approve the attached
  resolutions approving the Projects and directing staff to file the Notices of Exemptions with the County Clerk.

  prevent the increase in the number of cases, now staff would like to start working on recovery efforts for Lynwood

  2. Financial assistance pre-paid cards for residents who fell below the federal poverty level prior to the
  COVID-19 crisis and have now fallen into a deeper economic hardship.
  3. Upskilling training program that is funded by the City for residents who are currently unemployed and
  preparing them to enter a more technologically advanced workforce.

  Upskilling/Reskilling Workforce Training Program
  The City will collaborate with different agencies to provide an Upskilling/Reskilling Workforce Training Program
  for the residents of Lynwood with priority given to those that are unemployed. The mission would be to educate,
  train, and develop workers for growth and advancement in the workplace. Upskilling would focus on improving a
  person's skills so they could continue to work within the same job field. The emphasis for upskilling would be to
  promote training and advancement practices to help workers progress in their careers and move into better-
  paying jobs. Reskilling would focus on learning new skills, so a person could do a different job. The emphasis for
  reskilling would be the development of significantly different skills to make someone suitable for amore
  technologically advanced job as we recover from the COVID-19 crisis.

  Relief programs offered to Lynwood residents will be funded by the City with no obligation for repayment from those who

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled, “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD APPROVING FY 2019-20 BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS
  AMENDING THE FY 2019-20 ADOPTED BUDGET HERETO ATTACHED AS SCHEDULE A”.

  Background:

  On July 2, 2019, the City Council adopted the FY 2019-20 budget and approved the FY 2020-21 budget. The FY
  2019-21 budget is the City’s financial operating plan that establishes the City’s goals, budget priorities, and
  desired service levels for the fiscal year, as well as identifies the fiscal resources necessary to achieve them. The
  adopted budget was based on certain assumptions and meeting expenditure and revenue projections.

  Discussion and Analysis:

  During the fiscal year, there are circumstances that arise that require changes to departmental adopted budgets.
  At the beginning of each fiscal, the City Council authorizes appropriations of monies which are allocated at the
  fund and department level. Budget adjustments require changes to the initial authorized appropriations, therefore,
  requiring the approval of the City Council. Staff is recommending that the City Council authorize the approval of
  the identified budget adjustments and amend the FY 2019-20 adopted budget accordingly.

  FY 2019-20 Departmental Budget Adjustment Requests

  Staff is presenting the following Budget Adjustments for Council’s consideration to amend the FY 2019-20 budget
  for the General Fund and others.

  1. City Clerk Operational Budget ($7,950 – General Fund) – An additional appropriation in the amount of
  $7,950 from General Fund reserves, is needed to cover departmental invoice(s) for agenda management
  software.

   2. Community Development Operational Budget ($6,739 – General Fund; $1,070,239 – All Funds) – An
  additional appropriation in the amount of $1,070,239 ($6,739 from General Fund reserves, $6,500 from Urban
  Farming (Cannabis) Fund reserves, and $1,057,000 from Community Development Housing A Fund reserves) is
  needed to cover increase in public relations contract, membership dues, stipends, and costs related to housing
  projects.

  3.  Human Resources Operational Budget ($51,563 – General Fund) – An additional appropriation of
  $51,563 from General Fund reserves, is needed to cover the cost to update the City’s Natural Hazards Mitigation

  4. Public Works Operational Budget ($101,385 – General Fund; $1,346,293 – All Funds) – An additional
  appropriation in the amount of $1,346,293 ($101,385 from General Fund reserves, $53,000 from Refuse Fund
  reserves, $56,425 from Traffic Safety Fund reserves, $7,000 from Lighting Maintenance Fund Reserves,
  $823,920 from LUA 2020 A Revenue Bonds , and $304,563 from 2017 Lease Revenue Bonds) is needed to

  trucks, equipment, safety gear, water quality and sewer services, etc.

  The Proposed FY 2019-20 Budget Adjustments are listed in Schedule A.

  Covid-19 Pandemic Impact

  In light of the need to adjust operational budget for department to continue to operate at the expected level, it is
  understood that the current Covid-19 pandemic can and will impact the City’s anticipated revenue for the current
  and future fiscal years. Staff proactively called the top 25 businesses within the city to ascertain a sense of the
  impact of Covid-19. It is anticipated that the City will see a potential 13.3% drop in General Fund revenue for the
  current fiscal year due to the current pandemic. The 13.3% drop ($4,308,150) in revenue reflects a $1,308,150
  decrease in sales tax and Measure P.S. revenue as well as an anticipated loss of $3,000,000 revenue in
  sale/lease back water tower revenue. Ultimately, there will be a substantial impact the City’s major revenue
  sources such as Sales Tax, Measure R, Measure M, and SB1 (Gas Tax).

  adjustment total impact to the General Fund is $167,637.
